images.title: Jumps for 14 and 36
images.purpose: Show that the jump sizes that land on both 14 and 36 are their common factors, 1 and 2.
images.composition: One centred row of four big tiles with a short label above and one line below, lots of white space.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 4 equal square tiles with equal gaps showing the factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Tiles 1 and 2 are reddish purple #CC79A7; tiles 7 and 14 are teal #0072B2. A thin grey #6B7280 bracket under tiles 1 and 2 only. Exactly 4 tiles, 1 bracket.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Only 1 and 2 are factors of both 14 and 36.
images.description: Four tiles for the factors of 14, with 1 and 2 in purple and bracketed because they also divide 36.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the bracketed tiles and say why 7 does not land on 36.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture carries the main idea of this concept.
